story.iWant: to automatically install missing development dependencies
story.soThat: users can set up the complete development environment without manual intervention
story.tasks: 1. Node.js Installation Engine, 2. Python Installation Engine, 3. Git Installation and Configuration, 4. Package Manager Setup, 5. Progress Feedback and Error Handling, 6. Installation Verification, 7. Integration Testing

story-context.acceptanceCriteria: 1. Implement automatic installation of Node.js (LTS version) for Windows/macOS/Linux, 2. Implement automatic installation of Python 3.8+ for Windows/macOS/Linux, 3. Implement automatic Git installation and basic configuration, 4. Support package manager installation (npm, pip) and initial setup, 5. Provide installation progress feedback and error handling for failed installations, 6. Verify installation success and update system environment variables

doc.title: Operating System Detection and Platform Adaptation
doc.snippet: Platform-specific path handling and file operations, system information collection functionality for environment diagnostics

doc.title: Development Environment Dependency Check
doc.section: Dependency checking architecture and data structures
doc.snippet: Create DependencyChecker class in core/dependency_checker.py, implement network status checker in utils/network_utils.py

doc.title: One-Click Launch Architecture
doc.snippet: Platform-specific installation methods, elevation handling, security requirements for package verification

artifact.reason: Reuse dependency detection results for installation planning
Use network connectivity checking for download operations
Integrate with existing OS detection for platform-specific installations

story-context.constraints: - Platform-Specific Installation: Use appropriate installation methods for each OS (Windows installers, macOS Homebrew, Linux package managers) - Elevation Handling: Request administrator privileges only when necessary for system-wide installations - Idempotent Operations: Design installations to be safe to run multiple times - Rollback Capability: Maintain ability to undo partial installations if errors occur - Security: Verify downloaded packages using official sources and checksums - Service-based architecture with dedicated classes for each functionality - Follow existing dependency injection and configuration patterns

interface.name: NodeJSInstaller
interface.signature: class NodeJSInstaller: def __init__(self, os_detector, network_utils); def install(self, version='lts') -> bool

interface.name: PythonInstaller
interface.signature: class PythonInstaller: def __init__(self, os_detector, network_utils); def install(self, min_version='3.8') -> bool

interface.name: GitInstaller
interface.signature: class GitInstaller: def __init__(self, os_detector, network_utils); def install_and_configure(self) -> bool

interface.name: PackageManagerSetup
interface.signature: class PackageManagerSetup: def configure_npm(self) -> bool; def configure_pip(self) -> bool

interface.name: ProgressTracker
interface.signature: class ProgressTracker: def start_installation(self, component: str); def update_progress(self, progress: int); def complete_installation(self, success: bool)

interface.name: InstallationVerifier
interface.signature: class InstallationVerifier: def verify_nodejs(self) -> bool; def verify_python(self) -> bool; def verify_git(self) -> bool

tests.standards: Mock installation testing without actual software installation, integration testing for complete workflows, platform-specific testing across Windows/macOS/Linux, error scenario testing for network failures and permission errors, progress reporting verification

test.idea: Test NodeJSInstaller.download_and_install() method with mocked download
Test PythonInstaller.install() method with different OS platforms
Test GitInstaller.install_and_configure() with mocked system calls
